jurisdiction.venue: Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC), Sydney

headline: Australia’s Big Four Logged 35 Statutory Audit Red Flags — and Their Regulator Still Can’t License the Firms
deck: ASIC’s compulsory review of internal complaints at Deloitte, EY, KPMG, and PwC surfaced allegations of unverified assets, copy-pasted audit files, and whistleblower retaliation—yet the watchdog can only refer accountants and ask Treasury for powers.

financials.amount_display: 94% of ASX Market Cap & 85% of Super Funds Audited

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: ASIC Report 848 reviewed 558 responsive internal complaints across Deloitte, EY, KPMG, and PwC (2023–2026) and identified 35 raising statutory audit misconduct or client-confidentiality concerns, while noting ASIC still lacks statutory power to license or directly regulate audit firms.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: Inspecting four garages that certify 94% of the city’s bridges, finding 35 internal whistleblower complaints about unchecked bolts, and realizing your permit system only covers individual mechanics
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: Immediate facility audit and licensing suspension in regulated safety trades, versus de-identified summaries and referrals to industry associations here

sources.title: 26-292MR ASIC complaints probe uncovers potential audit-related issues at Big Four
REP 848: ASIC’s review of internal complaints at major audit firms

interactive_art_spec.caption: Sydney’s central business district skyline at sunset. Deloitte, EY, KPMG, and PwC audit more than 94% of Australia’s listed market capitalisation and over 85% of superannuation entities, yet remain outside firm-level ASIC licensing.
